metrics.name: 1. Storage Efficiency (Storage Consumption)
metrics.scope: This design's own tracker.py only; shared application code, assets, dependencies and builds are excluded.

evidence.scope: This design's tracker.py source file only; not standalone application or installed storage.

metrics.name: 2. Performance (Latency)
metrics.statistic: Mean successful simulated input-to-display latency; P50/P95 and failures are retained in evidence.
metrics.scope: Actual simulated-angle control click to matching DOM feedback plus two animation-frame callbacks; physical ESP32 transport and pixel presentation are excluded.

evidence.aggregation: Pooled successful raw sample observations across repeats; failed samples remain in counts.

metrics.name: 3. Maintainability (Maintainability Index Score)
metrics.scope: This design's own tracker.py only; no frontend or whole-application score is claimed.

evidence.scope: This design's tracker.py Python file only; not a whole-application Maintainability Index.
evidence.method: Radon mi_visit(source, multi=True), per-file 0-100 Maintainability Index

metrics.name: 4. Memory Efficiency (RAM Consumption)
metrics.statistic: Mean sampled browser plus Python backend process-tree RSS; sampled peak and failures are retained in evidence.
metrics.scope: Resident/working-set sum in decimal MB; shared pages may be counted more than once, and sampling can miss short peaks.

evidence.statistic: sum of process-tree RSS / working sets
evidence.shared_page_caveat: Shared pages may be counted in more than one process; this is not unique physical RAM. Sampled peaks can miss shorter allocation spikes.
evidence.aggregation: Pooled successful raw sample observations across repeats; failed samples remain in counts.

metrics.name: 5. Computational Efficiency (CPU Utilization)
metrics.statistic: Mean CPU utilization weighted by observed interval duration, normalized across logical CPUs; sampled P95, peak and failures are retained in evidence.
metrics.scope: Owned browser and Python backend process groups while the selected design runs; percent of total logical CPU capacity, not whole-system CPU utilization or a physical ESP32 measurement.

evidence.statistic: process-tree user + system CPU time / interval wall time / logical CPU count * 100
evidence.normalization: 100% means all logical CPU capacity; one fully busy logical CPU is 100 / logical_cpu_count percent
evidence.mean_statistic: interval-duration-weighted mean of normalized CPU percentages
evidence.p95_statistic: P95 of sampled interval percentages (linear interpolation)
evidence.process_lifetime_caveat: New processes are baselined at first sighting; CPU consumed before that sighting or after the last sighting of an exited process is not recoverable. Short-lived processes entirely between samples can be missed.
evidence.graphics_caveat: This headless benchmark uses SwiftShader software rendering, so browser CPU includes software graphics work; remeasure with the final GPU configuration or Electron package.
evidence.aggregation: Pooled successful raw intervals across repeats; mean is weighted by interval duration, while P95 and peak describe sampled intervals; failed samples remain in counts.
